name: Tuxedo
description: Tuxedo is a card-capturing game invented by George Parker, played with a 56-card Rook deck (no Rook card). 4 cards per player + 4 face-up in the 'pond'. Capture by matching number or matching sums. Sweeps (clearing the pond) score bonus. 'Orange' call bonus for capturing red+yellow together. First to 100 wins.

content.text: Tuxedo is a card-capturing game invented by George Parker, played with a 56-card Rook deck (no Rook card). 4 cards per player + 4 face-up in the 'pond'. Capture by matching number or matching sums. Sweeps (clearing the pond) score bonus. 'Orange' call bonus for capturing red+yellow together. First to 100 wins.

Tuxedo is an American Casino variant often attributed to George Parker (Parker Brothers). It is played by 2 to 6 players using a Rook deck, with mechanics matching American or Royal Casino and distinct scoring: most cards, orange captures (red and yellow together), sweeps, and fives; first to 100 wins. The HOYLE Card Games collection includes a Tuxedo program.
56-card Rook deck (no Rook card). 4 colors, values 1-14.
4 each + 4 face-up (pond). Redeal 4 when hands empty.
